title: SLA-aligned scaling engine: percentile-based targets with conservative unwind
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a new autoscaling policy engine variant that targets SLA percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for request latency and sustained throughput targets simultaneously. The engine must ensure conservative unwind behavior to avoid oscillation and protect dedicated fleets from cost overruns or cascading evictions. This ticket covers spec, proto config, simulator tests, and an initial canary rollout on a restricted tenant set.
acceptance_criteria: Policy config accepts multiple target metrics (latency percentile + sustained RPS) and a prioritized objective list
Simulator shows <3% SLA violations under synthetic burst patterns used by SRE test harness
Scaling step limits and decay parameters prevent more than 20% oscillation on a 30m window in production traces
Canary rollout verifies safe scale-down with explicit workload quiesce signals and no dropped requests for 48h
Design doc reviewed by PM and SRE; implementation PR merged with unit + integration tests
proposed_design: Introduce "quantile_targeter" as a first-class component: it computes target capacity from observed latency percentiles using a mapping table per model/instance-type. Combine with a separate sustained_throughput_estimator that uses a time-weighted EMA to smooth short bursts. The scaler composes targets: primary objective (p95 latency) yields a minimum capacity; secondary objective (sustained throughput) yields a desired capacity. Final scaling decision clamps by safety fences: max_step_pct, min_capacity, max_capacity_by_contract, and derivative_limit. Implement conservative_unwind: when traffic decreases, only allow scale-down at a slower rate (decay_factor) and require a quiet window (quiet_period) before aggressive downsizing. Persist short-term headroom credits per tenant to permit temporary spikes without immediate scale-up, and reconcile credits every 5m with billing/rate-limiter signals.
rollout_plan: Run simulator across 3 months of production traces to validate stability metrics
Deploy to staging; run synthetic burst suite and runbook dry-run
Canary to 5 low-risk Dedicated tenants for 72h, monitor cost/latency/cancel-counts
Gradual 25/50/100% migration with rollback knobs and automated fallback to current governor
risks: Incorrect quantile mapping could overprovision and increase tenant costs
Too-aggressive unwind might cause oscillation and SLA breaches during variable workloads
Interaction with existing cache-prefetch and KV cache warmers could create coupling bugs
Edge cases around tenant isolation and per-tenant max_capacity caps need careful gating
comments: 2025-01-16 Aisha Patel: Initial spec added. Primary goal is to reduce p95 SLA violations without big cost increases. Added mapping idea for percentile->capacity.

2025-01-20 Riley Chen: Prototype quantile_targeter implemented in simulator repo. Observed reduced false positives vs simple thresholding. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/412
2025-01-24 Morgan Lee (SRE): Simulator looks promising but worried about scale-down speed. Recommend conservative_unwind with default decay_factor=0.5 and quiet_period=15m.
2025-01-28 Priya Nair (PM): Aligning with Dedicated capacity SLA language in contract template. Need a per-tenant max_capacity_by_contract check early in the decision pipeline.
2025-02-01 Riley Chen: Added derivative limiter: max_derivative_pct=10%/5m and max_step_pct=30%. Integration tests added. Staging run shows <1.8% p95 violations on our burst suite.
